title: Severe allocation shortfall
evidence: Planned quantity 348,922 vs allocated quantity 34,126; shortage_quantity 314,796; fill_rate_percent 9.78%.
recommended_action: Conduct an immediate review of allocation rules and increase allocated quantity to achieve at least 50% of planned volume.
rationale: The extreme shortfall directly drives the low service level and high lost sales, representing the most urgent risk.
expected_business_effect: Higher fill rate and service level, reduction in lost sales.

title: Service level far below target
evidence: Service level percent 7.45% (Baseline) and 6.57% (Disruption) versus service_level_target_percent 95.0% (assumption).
recommended_action: Implement demand prioritization for high‑priority SKUs and expedite shipments for those items.
rationale: Improving the proportion of demand fulfilled will move the service level toward the target and mitigate lost sales.
expected_business_effect: Improved customer service metrics and reduced revenue leakage.

title: Increased disruption impact on deliveries
evidence: Failed deliveries rise from 3 (Baseline) to 17 (Disruption); total_unreceived_quantity increases from 1,062 to 7,469.
recommended_action: Develop a contingency logistics plan that includes alternative transport routes and backup carriers for critical shipments.
rationale: The disruption scenario shows a sharp degradation in delivery reliability, indicating vulnerability to external shocks.
expected_business_effect: Reduced variability in fulfillment during disruptions and higher resilience.

title: Large allocation gaps for top‑gap products
evidence: Top product P033 gap 5,763; P055 gap 4,613; P072 gap 5,252; etc., as shown in top_products list.
recommended_action: Prioritize supplemental sourcing (e.g., secondary suppliers or expedited production) for the top‑gap products.
rationale: These products represent the highest demand exposure; closing their gaps will quickly improve overall service.
expected_business_effect: Targeted reduction in out‑of‑stock incidents for high‑impact SKUs.

title: Limited supplier redundancy
evidence: Supplier allocation rows 102 for 100 replenishment products, indicating minimal excess supplier capacity.
recommended_action: Qualify and onboard additional suppliers for products with the largest gaps and highest risk scores.
rationale: Increasing the supplier base reduces reliance on a narrow set of sources and improves resilience to supplier failures.
expected_business_effect: Enhanced supply continuity and lower disruption risk.

title: Missing risk multiplier data in allocation model
evidence: supplier_allocation_columns include risk_multiplier, but no values are provided in the dataset.
recommended_action: Capture and integrate risk_multiplier values for each supplier into the allocation model.
rationale: Risk‑adjusted unit costs enable more informed trade‑offs between cost and resilience.
expected_business_effect: More balanced allocation decisions that reflect supplier risk.
